tool.name: code_graph_find_definition
tool.description: Find where a symbol is defined in the indexed source tree. Returns file:line for each matching declaration. Use this BEFORE grepping when you need to navigate from a usage to the implementation — one tool call instead of repository-wide search. Symbol matching uses substring containment, so partial names work (e.g. "checkCustomerAccountPermission" matches the full SCIP moniker).

parameter.name: symbol
parameter.description: Symbol name to locate (function, class, type, exported binding). Bare identifier preferred.

returns.description: {"output": "<name> defined at file:line:col"} for each match. {"output": "code graph not available..."} when the indexer was skipped for this target. {"output": "no definition matches found..."} when the symbol isn't in the index.

tool.notes: - The index is pre-built at sandbox setup; queries are read-only and fast. - Returns up to 50 matches. - Falls back to chunk-range location for re-exports / barrel files where SCIP doesn't record a precise enclosing range. - On missing index (eg. unsupported language), output explains the situation — proceed with search_files / read_file instead.
tool.examples:
# Locate the implementation of a middleware
checkCustomerAccountPermission

tool.name: code_graph_find_references
tool.description: Return every place a symbol is referenced in the indexed tree. This is the highest-value query for structural security review: "which routes mount this middleware", "everywhere this auth helper is called", "what depends on this config flag". One call replaces an org-wide grep + manual sift.

parameter.name: symbol
parameter.description: Symbol name to find references for. Bare identifier preferred.

parameter.name: include_definition
parameter.description: Include the definition site in the results. Default false (most callers want references only).

returns.description:
{"output": "<name> — N occurrence(s):
 file:line
 file:line
..."} grouped by matched name (substring matches that resolved to different symbols are listed separately). Capped at 50 results.

tool.notes: - Use for "find all callers of X" questions. Don't grep first if you can ask this. - Locations are chunk-level (line ranges) rather than column-precise — read the file for the specific line if needed. - When the symbol appears in multiple SCIP monikers (eg. similarly-named exports across files), results are grouped by display name so you can see each cluster.
tool.examples:
# Find every place a middleware is mounted on a route
authorizeToParticipantAndAdminRole
# Include the def site too
authorizeToParticipantAndAdminRole true

tool.name: code_graph_find_implementations
tool.description: Return implementations / subtypes of an interface or abstract type. Reads SCIP `Relationship` records where `is_implementation=true` points at the target. Use this when you have an interface or abstract class and want to know every class that implements / extends it — one tool call instead of grepping for `implements X` / `extends X` across the tree.

parameter.name: interface
parameter.description: Interface, trait, or abstract class name. Bare identifier preferred.

returns.description: {"output": "<impl_name> implements <interface> at file:line\n..."} per implementor. Empty when nothing implements it (or when the indexer didn't emit Relationship records for that language).

tool.notes: - Best for object-oriented languages where SCIP indexers emit Relationship records (TypeScript, Go interface satisfaction, Python ABCs, Rust traits). - If the result is unexpectedly empty, the language indexer may not have emitted is_implementation for that symbol — fall back to find_references on the interface name + manual filter.
tool.examples:
# Find every Auth strategy class in the tree
AuthorizationStrategy

tool.name: code_graph_list_symbols
tool.description: List symbols defined under a file or directory path. Useful for "what's in this module" triage without reading the whole file — returns symbol name + definition file:line per row. Saves tokens vs reading the entire file when you only need the structural shape.

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: File path (e.g. `src/auth/middlewares.ts`) or directory prefix (e.g. `src/auth/`). Path is relative to repo root.

returns.description: {"output": "<file>:\n <symbol> (line N)\n..."} grouped by file. Up to 50 symbols.

tool.notes: - For a quick map of a router/middleware/service module, this beats reading the whole file. - Returns only DEFINED symbols (functions, classes, methods, exports). For references TO those symbols use code_graph_find_references. - Path is prefix-matched, so `src/auth/` lists everything under that dir; `src/auth/middlewares.ts` lists symbols in that single file.
tool.examples:
# Map out an auth module before drilling in
src/auth/
# Just one file's defined symbols
src/withdrawals/router.ts

tool.name: code_graph_get_imports
tool.description: List the symbols referenced from a given source file. Approximates "what does this file depend on" without reading the whole file. Useful for triaging a router or middleware file before drilling in.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path from the repo root (eg. src/withdrawals/router.ts).

returns.description:
{"output": "<file> references:
 name1
 name2
..."} — distinct symbols mentioned in the file, sorted.

tool.notes: - Superset of declared imports (includes in-file uses of globals). - Capped at 50 distinct symbols.

tool.name: code_graph_grep
tool.description: Resolve a symbol precisely via the code graph, then show its SOURCE — the definition's full body plus each reference site with surrounding context. This is the tool to use when you need to SEE THE CODE, not just locations: "show me where checkAuth is defined and everywhere it's called, with the surrounding lines". One call replaces code_graph_find_references followed by a fan-out of read_file. Unlike grep it returns ZERO false hits from comments, string literals, vendored dependencies, or unrelated same-named symbols — every line shown is a real definition or reference of THIS symbol. Use this for security review when you need to judge logic (is there a bypassable check between source and sink?) rather than just enumerate call sites.

parameter.name: symbol
parameter.description: Symbol name to resolve and show. Bare identifier preferred (substring match handles language-specific monikers, same as the other code_graph_* tools).

parameter.name: context
parameter.description: Lines of source shown above and below each REFERENCE site. Default 3, max 10. The DEFINITION is always shown in full (its enclosing body), regardless of this value.

returns.description:
{"output": "# <name>
● DEFINITION file:line
 <numbered source lines of the def body>

# references (N shown, ±C lines)
● REFERENCE file:line
 <numbered source window>
..."}. {"output": "code graph not available..."} when the indexer was skipped. {"output": "no symbol matches..."} when the symbol isn't indexed.

tool.notes: - Prefer this over `code_graph_find_references` + multiple `read_file` calls when you need to read the code around each hit — it's one call and far fewer tokens than reading whole files. - Reference sites are capped at 15 (each costs a source window); the definition body is shown in full but truncated at 120 lines for generated/minified files. - Falls back to a bare location line for any hit whose source file can't be read (it still tells you where to look). - For a plain location list (no source), use `code_graph_find_references`. For just the def location, use `code_graph_find_definition`.
tool.examples:
# See an auth middleware's implementation AND every place it guards, with context
checkCustomerAccountPermission
# Wider window around each call site
validateWithdrawal 5

tool.name: code_graph_get_symbol_at
tool.description: Return symbols mentioned in the chunk containing a given line in a file. Coarser than IDE go-to-symbol (chunk-level, not cursor-precise) but useful for "what does this code reference" lookups.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path from the repo root.

parameter.name: line
parameter.description: Line number (0-indexed, matching how SCIP encodes positions).

returns.description:
{"output": "<file>:<line> mentions:
 name1
 name2
..."} — distinct symbols in the same chunk as that line.

tool.notes: - SCIP chunks are line ranges, not individual lines — expect multiple symbols per call. - Use code_graph_find_references afterwards to drill into a specific symbol's other usages.
